rawInput.answer: Routes are registered via RouterGroup methods (GET/POST/etc. in routergroup.go) which call `handle()` → `group.engine.addRoute()` (gin.go), inserting the path into a per-HTTP-method radix ("Patricia") tree (`methodTrees`/`node.addRoute` in tree.go). Incoming requests are matched in `Engine.ServeHTTP` → `handleHTTPRequest` (gin.go), which looks up the tree for the request's HTTP method and calls `node.getValue(path, ...)` (tree.go) to walk the radix tree, extract path params, and return the matched handler chain, which is then executed via `c.Next()`.

turns.question: How are route parameters like :name captured during tree matching?
toolCalls:
other: {"answer":"During insertion (`node.insertChild`, tree.go), `findWildcard` scans a path segment for a leading `:` or `*`. A `:name` segment becomes its own child node with `nType: param` and `path` set to `":name"` (the wildcard token itself, including the colon), with `wildChild: true` set on the parent so the router knows to try a wildcard child when no static index matches. `*name` catch-all segments get a similar dedicated `catchAll` node.

During matching (`node.getValue`, tree.go), the walker first tries to match static children via `n.indices` (a byte per literal next-char). When no static index matches and `n.wildChild` is true, it descends into the wildcard child (always the last entry in `n.children`). For a `param` node, it scans forward until the next `/` or end of string to find the segment boundary, then appends a `Param{Key: n.path[1:], Value: path[:end]}` (stripping the leading `:`) into the `Params` slice passed in by the caller — optionally URL-unescaping the value if `unescape` is set. For a `catchAll` node it does the same but captures everything up to the end of the path. These captured `Params` are returned in `nodeValue.params` and copied onto `Context.Params` in `handleHTTPRequest`, so handlers can read them via `c.Param("name")`.

A `skippedNodes` stack also lets the walker backtrack: if a static-child match fails deeper in the tree, it can roll back to a previously skipped wildcard node (and truncate `params` back to that node's recorded `paramsCount`) before trying the wildcard branch — this is what allows routes like `/users/:id` and `/users/new` to coexist and be matched correctly regardless of insertion/lookup order.</answer>

rawInput.answer: Routes are registered via RouterGroup methods (GET/POST/etc. in routergroup.go) which call `handle()` → `group.engine.addRoute()` (gin.go), inserting the path into a per-HTTP-method radix ("Patricia") tree (`methodTrees`/`node.addRoute` in tree.go). Incoming requests are matched in `Engine.ServeHTTP` → `handleHTTPRequest` (gin.go), which looks up the tree for the request's HTTP method and calls `node.getValue(path, ...)` (tree.go) to walk the radix tree, extract path params, and return the matched handler chain, which is then executed via `c.Next()`.

report.answer:
During insertion (`node.insertChild`, tree.go), `findWildcard` scans a path segment for a leading `:` or `*`. A `:name` segment becomes its own child node with `nType: param` and `path` set to `":name"` (the wildcard token itself, including the colon), with `wildChild: true` set on the parent so the router knows to try a wildcard child when no static index matches. `*name` catch-all segments get a similar dedicated `catchAll` node.

During matching (`node.getValue`, tree.go), the walker first tries to match static children via `n.indices` (a byte per literal next-char). When no static index matches and `n.wildChild` is true, it descends into the wildcard child (always the last entry in `n.children`). For a `param` node, it scans forward until the next `/` or end of string to find the segment boundary, then appends a `Param{Key: n.path[1:], Value: path[:end]}` (stripping the leading `:`) into the `Params` slice passed in by the caller — optionally URL-unescaping the value if `unescape` is set. For a `catchAll` node it does the same but captures everything up to the end of the path. These captured `Params` are returned in `nodeValue.params` and copied onto `Context.Params` in `handleHTTPRequest`, so handlers can read them via `c.Param("name")`.

A `skippedNodes` stack also lets the walker backtrack: if a static-child match fails deeper in the tree, it can roll back to a previously skipped wildcard node (and truncate `params` back to that node's recorded `paramsCount`) before trying the wildcard branch — this is what allows routes like `/users/:id` and `/users/new` to coexist and be matched correctly regardless of insertion/lookup order.
